The *Maṇiratanaṅgapañha* ("The Jewel Treasure", Mil 7.7.7) is a discourse unit within the *Milindapañha*, located in the late Pali collection [SuttaCentral]. The text belongs to the simile-driven discourses of the work, drawing doctrinal lessons from the qualities of a precious jewel (*maṇiratana*) [SuttaCentral]. SuttaCentral links or references the text in connection with the *Kapilasutta* of the Sutta Nipāta (Snp 2.6 / PTS Snp 49), and lists three translations in three languages [SuttaCentral].
Textual reuse data generated by DharmaNexus demonstrates that the text shares extensive formulaic and structural parallels with other similes in the *Milindapañha*, totaling 228 matching passages across 41 Pali texts [DharmaNexus]. Its most significant internal overlaps occur with other sections of the work, including the *Āpaṅgapañha* (Mil 7.4.2), the *Pavanaṅgapañha* (Mil 7.7.4), the *Sūriyaṅgapañha* (Mil 7.4.8), and the *Māgavikaṅgapañha* (Mil 7.7.8) [DharmaNexus]. Across traditions, DharmaNexus registers minor automated alignments with the Tibetan translation of the *Aṣṭasāhasrikā Prajñāpāramitā* (D0012), though these are machine matches rather than verified historical parallels [DharmaNexus].
